notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION FIXTURE. Generic drafting language written for offline testing. It is not derived from any Tessera or client agreement, is not an adopted playbook, and requires qualified counsel before any use. These clauses exist because the structure memo recommends positions in each of these areas — titles, triggering events, valuation, buy-sell, buy-out payment, work product, and tax distributions — and a memo that promises a position the assembled document does not contain is worse than one that promises nothing.

clauses.title: Titles and Authority
clauses.absence_risk: Titles get handed out casually in founder-led businesses and then get relied on. Without this, a counterparty can argue that a person carrying a title had authority the agreement never granted, and a member can argue the title carried economics.

variants.when: Every entity where anyone carries a title. One sentence, and it closes an entire category of argument.
variants.trade_off: None. This clause is not negotiated.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the titles actually used on cards, signature blocks, and filings are covered — an unlisted title is the one that causes the problem.
variants.text: **{n}. Titles.** The Members may adopt titles for use in the conduct of the Company's business. No title, however designated, confers authority, voting power, economic entitlement, or Percentage Interest beyond that expressly granted by this Agreement, and no Person dealing with the Company is entitled to rely on a title as evidence of authority to bind the Company.

clauses.title: Triggering Events
clauses.absence_risk: Without triggering events, death, disability, divorce, bankruptcy, or a member simply walking away leaves that member's full economic and voting rights intact, in the hands of whoever now holds them.

defines.definition: Each event listed in the Triggering Events section of this Agreement, in each case with respect to the Member to whom it relates.

The inability of a Member, due to physical or mental incapacity, substantially to perform such Member's duties to the Company for either (i) {disability_consecutive_days} consecutive days or (ii) {disability_aggregate_days} days in any trailing period of {disability_window_days} days, as reasonably determined by the other Members in good faith and, if disputed, confirmed by a licensed physician mutually acceptable to the Members.

variants.when: Closely held entities generally. Each event is a moment where an owner stops being the person the others went into business with.
variants.trade_off: The breach and conviction triggers are the ones a counterparty resists. The divorce trigger is often the one that matters most and is the one founders are least comfortable discussing.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the Disability definition against any disability policy the Company or the Members carry — a mismatch leaves a funding gap precisely when the obligation triggers. Confirm the divorce trigger's interaction with community-property law in the governing jurisdiction, and whether spousal consents should be obtained at signing. Confirm whether “moral turpitude” is enforceable as a standard in the governing jurisdiction.

variants.when: Where the counterparty will not accept conduct-based triggers and the relationship does not warrant pressing.
variants.trade_off: LESS protective. Dropping the breach and conviction triggers means a member who damages the business keeps every right they had, and the only remedy is a damages claim.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the Members understand what has been given up. Consider retaining the breach trigger even where the conviction trigger is dropped.

clauses.title: Fair Market Value
clauses.absence_risk: A buy-out right with no valuation method is a lawsuit with extra steps. The parties reach the moment they most need a number and have no agreed way to produce one.

defines.definition: The value of a Membership Interest determined in accordance with the Fair Market Value section of this Agreement.

variants.when: Wherever the Agreement requires a purchase at Fair Market Value. The convergence rule settles most cases without a third appraiser and without litigation.
variants.trade_off: Appraisal is slower and costlier than a formula, but a formula that was right at formation is usually wrong by the time it is needed.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm whether the appraiser is instructed to apply, or to disregard, discounts for lack of marketability and lack of control. This single instruction can move the price by a third and is the most commonly litigated omission in buy-sell provisions. The clause below is deliberately silent so the instruction is a conscious choice.
variants.text: **{n}. Fair Market Value.** Where this Agreement requires a purchase at Fair Market Value, the Members shall first attempt to agree on Fair Market Value within {fmv_agreement_days} days. If they cannot agree, each Member shall, within a further {fmv_appraiser_days} days, select a qualified independent business appraiser. The two appraisers shall jointly determine Fair Market Value within {fmv_determination_days} days. If the two determinations are within {fmv_convergence_percent} of each other, Fair Market Value is the average of the two. If the determinations differ by more than {fmv_convergence_percent}, the two appraisers shall jointly select a third independent appraiser whose determination of Fair Market Value is final and binding. Each Member bears the cost of its own appraiser; the cost of any third appraiser is shared equally.

clauses.title: Buy-Sell Procedure
clauses.absence_risk: Without a buy-sell procedure, a triggering event creates a right to buy with no mechanism to exercise it, no price, and no closing.

variants.when: Two equal principals with comparable liquidity. Naming a price without knowing which side of the trade you will end up on is what makes the price honest.
variants.trade_off: A shotgun favours whoever can write the cheque. Where liquidity is asymmetric — a passive investor, an unequal cap table — it becomes an option held by the deeper pocket, and appraisal-based valuation is the fairer mechanism.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm both parties can realistically fund a purchase at a plausible price. Confirm the deemed-election default on failure to respond is intended, and consider whether the offeror should be required to demonstrate financing before serving the notice.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Offer Notice.** Upon a Triggering Event other than death or Disability, or upon a Deadlock that has reached the buy-sell step, the Member invoking this Section (the “Offeror”) shall deliver written notice to the other Member (the “Offeree”) stating a single price per one percent (1%) of Percentage Interest at which the Offeror is willing either to buy the Offeree's entire Membership Interest or to sell the Offeror's entire Membership Interest to the Offeree, at the Offeree's election.

**{n}.2 Offeree Election.** Within {buysell_election_days} days of the Offer Notice, the Offeree shall elect, by written notice to the Offeror, either (i) to sell the Offeree's entire Membership Interest to the Offeror at the stated price, or (ii) to purchase the Offeror's entire Membership Interest at the same stated price. Failure to elect within such period is deemed an election under clause (i).

**{n}.3 Closing.** Closing of the purchase shall occur within {buysell_closing_days} days of the Offeree's election or deemed election, on the payment terms set out in Section {ref:gov-buyout-payment}.

**{n}.4 Death or Disability.** Upon the death or Disability of a Member, the other Member (or the Company, at the other Member's election) has the right, but not the obligation, exercisable by written notice within {death_election_days} days of the Triggering Event, to purchase all but not less than all of the affected Member's Membership Interest at Fair Market Value determined under Section {ref:gov-fair-market-value}, on the payment terms set out in Section {ref:gov-buyout-payment}. The Members may, but are not required to, fund this right through life or disability insurance owned by the Company or by the other Member, with premiums paid as the Members mutually agree.

variants.when: Where the parties do not have comparable liquidity — passive investors, an unequal cap table, or a materially different balance sheet on each side.
variants.trade_off: Slower and costlier than a shotgun, and it removes the pricing discipline the shotgun creates. It is nonetheless the only fair mechanism where one side cannot credibly fund a purchase.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the discount instruction to the appraiser, and confirm whether the Company or the remaining Members hold the purchase right — the tax consequences differ materially.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Purchase Right.** Upon a Triggering Event, the Members other than the Triggering Member (or the Company, at their election) have the right, but not the obligation, exercisable by written notice within {death_election_days} days of the Triggering Event, to purchase all but not less than all of the Triggering Member's Membership Interest at Fair Market Value determined under Section {ref:gov-fair-market-value}.

**{n}.2 Allocation.** If more than one Member elects to purchase, each purchasing Member acquires a portion of the offered interest in proportion to its Percentage Interest relative to the other purchasing Members, unless they agree otherwise in writing.

**{n}.3 Closing.** Closing shall occur within {buysell_closing_days} days of the exercise notice, on the payment terms set out in Section {ref:gov-buyout-payment}.

**{n}.4 Insurance.** The Members may, but are not required to, fund a purchase on death or Disability through insurance owned by the Company or by the Members, with premiums paid as the Members mutually agree.

clauses.title: Payment Terms and Withdrawal
clauses.absence_risk: A buy-out the buyer cannot fund is not a remedy. Without payment terms, every purchase right in the agreement is exercisable only by whoever happens to hold cash.

variants.when: Every buy-out right in the Agreement.
variants.trade_off: The seller carries credit risk on the note for the deferral period. The pledge of the acquired interest is what makes that risk tolerable.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the note terms against the applicable federal rate rules so the note is not recharacterised as carrying imputed interest, and confirm the pledge is perfected under the governing jurisdiction's Article 9. Consider whether the note should accelerate on a subsequent sale of the Company, and whether a pledge of the interest being purchased is adequate security.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Payment Terms.** Unless the parties to a purchase under this Agreement otherwise agree in writing, the purchase price shall be paid: (i) {buyout_cash_percent} in cash at closing; and (ii) the remainder pursuant to a promissory note issued by the purchasing party, bearing interest at the applicable federal rate in effect at closing, payable in equal monthly installments of principal and interest over {buyout_note_months} months, and secured by a pledge of the Membership Interest being acquired. The purchasing party may prepay the note in whole or in part at any time without penalty.

**{n}.2 Withdrawal from Management.** Effective upon the closing of any purchase of a Member's entire Membership Interest under this Agreement, the selling Member automatically ceases to be a Managing Member or Manager, has no further right to participate in the management of the Company, and shall execute such further documents as are reasonably necessary to evidence the Transfer and withdrawal.

**{n}.3 Continuing Obligations.** The selling Member's obligations under the confidentiality, restrictive covenant, and work product provisions of this Agreement survive the closing in accordance with their terms.

clauses.title: Tax Distributions and Tax Matters
clauses.absence_risk: Pass-through income is taxed to the member whether or not cash was distributed. Without a tax distribution, a profitable year can hand an owner a tax bill and no money to pay it.

variants.trade_off: A mandatory distribution competes with the business's own cash needs. The sufficient-cash qualifier is the usual compromise and is weaker than an unqualified obligation.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm the assumed tax rate and whether it should be the highest marginal combined rate applicable to any Member. Confirm the timing works against estimated-payment deadlines rather than only the annual filing date. Confirm the Partnership Representative designation and the limits on that person's authority to settle an audit.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Tax Distributions.** To the extent the Company has sufficient Available Cash, the Company shall distribute to each Member, no later than {tax_distribution_days} days after the end of each fiscal year, an amount sufficient to enable such Member to pay estimated and final federal and state income taxes attributable to such Member's allocable share of the Company's taxable income for that fiscal year, calculated at an assumed combined rate agreed by the Members. Tax distributions are treated as advances against, and reduce, subsequent distributions otherwise payable to that Member.

**{n}.2 Tax Classification.** The Company shall be treated as a partnership for federal and applicable state income tax purposes unless the Members unanimously elect otherwise.

**{n}.3 Partnership Representative.** The Members shall designate the “partnership representative” for purposes of Section 6223 of the Internal Revenue Code by mutual written agreement. The Partnership Representative shall keep the other Members reasonably informed of, and shall not settle or resolve, any material tax audit or proceeding without the other Members' consent.

**{n}.4 Tax Information.** The Company shall furnish each Member with a Schedule K-1 and such other information as is reasonably necessary for the Member's own tax filings within {tax_information_days} days after the end of each fiscal year.

clauses.title: Work Product and Intellectual Property
clauses.absence_risk: In a business whose value is how it thinks, the models, frameworks, and templates are the enterprise value. Without an assignment they belong to whoever wrote them and leave when that person does.

variants.when: Any business whose value is in method rather than in hard assets — advisory, capital, structuring, media, software.
variants.trade_off: A member who brought existing frameworks in will want them carved out. That carve-out should be a written schedule, not a verbal understanding.
variants.counsel_review: Confirm whether any Member is contributing pre-existing intellectual property that should be licensed rather than assigned, and schedule it. Confirm the present-assignment language is effective in the governing jurisdiction — an agreement to assign in the future is materially weaker than an assignment.
variants.text:
**{n}.1 Ownership.** All frameworks, deal structures, financial models, governance templates, methodologies, software, written materials, and other work product developed by a Member in connection with the Company's business is owned by the Company.

**{n}.2 Present Assignment.** Each Member hereby assigns to the Company all right, title, and interest in and to such work product, including all intellectual property rights therein, effective upon creation.

**{n}.3 Further Assurances.** Each Member shall execute such documents and take such further actions as are reasonably necessary to perfect, record, and enforce the Company's ownership under this Section.

**{n}.4 Pre-Existing Materials.** Materials owned by a Member prior to the Effective Date, and identified in writing to the other Members, are not assigned under this Section; the assigning Member grants the Company a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use such materials in the conduct of the Company's business.
